findings.title: Client-side upload limit is hardcoded to 10 MB
findings.body: The client validation replaces Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 MB limit. This ignores the configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb values, so users can attempt uploads that are not allowed (especially attachments), and configurations with limits above or below 10 MB are no longer respected in the UI.

findings.title: 413 error message uses a hardcoded 10 MB limit
findings.body: The 413 handler now reports a fixed 10 MB maximum size instead of using the relevant site setting. If the actual limit differs, users receive an inaccurate error message.

findings.title: Remote download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB
findings.body: FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of a site-setting-based limit for URL uploads. The later automatic downsizing only applies to recognized images, so non-image URL uploads, or images when the size setting is disabled, are no longer constrained by the configured limit at this stage.

findings.title: Upload proceeds even if the image is still too large after five attempts
findings.body: The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and then falls through without checking whether the file is now within SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. If the file is still oversized, or if re-encoding fails to reduce size, the code continues to Upload.create_for, risking an oversized stored image or an expensive delayed failure.

findings.title: In-place downsizing uses the same input and output path
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. ImageMagick or gifsicle may truncate or corrupt the file while reading and writing the same path, and the boolean return value is ignored. A failed conversion can therefore leave a corrupted or zero-byte upload that is then passed to Upload.create_for.

findings.title: SVG files are sent through raster downsizing
findings.body: The new block downsizes every file accepted by FileHelper.is_image?, but does not exclude SVG. Elsewhere, OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly copies SVGs instead of resizing them. Running ImageMagick convert on an SVG can rasterize or corrupt the vector image while keeping the original filename, producing a damaged upload.

findings.title: Animated-image handling depends on temporary file extension
findings.body: OptimizedImage.optimize selects the animated code path only when the input path ends in .gif. The controller downsizes temporary upload paths that may not preserve the original extension, so animated GIFs can be processed with convert file[0] and flattened to a single frame. The supplied '80%' dimension is also an ImageMagick-style geometry and may not be valid for gifsicle.

findings.title: Nil tempfile is not handled before calling tempfile.size
findings.body: If FileHelper.download fails, tempfile is nil because of rescue nil. The code then calls Upload.create_for with tempfile.size, which raises NoMethodError instead of returning a graceful upload error.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize method definitions break the previous API
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) definition replaces the preceding four-argument downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) definition. The old width/height API becomes dead code, and any existing caller using four positional size arguments will now pass the fourth argument as opts or raise an argument error.

findings.title: No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior
findings.body: The PR changes upload limits and mutates uploaded files, but adds no tests for the downsizing loop, failed conversions, files that remain oversized, SVG/GIF edge cases, or the changed OptimizedImage.downsize API. These are high-risk paths that can corrupt uploads or bypass configured limits.
